attempts.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: `blocker_moved` is wrong. The proposition means the cell in front of the door holds no ball (a ball carried in hand counts as moved, and a ball dropped back there makes it false again). The candidate scans the whole grid and returns true only when no ball exists anywhere, so a ball dropped elsewhere in the start room (the normal case per the example trace, where the ball is dropped away from the door) leaves `blocker_moved` false forever, and it can also spuriously go false if any unrelated ball exists. Necessary fix: locate the door cell in the grid, compute the cell in front of it (the door's outward side on the start-room side, e.g. the cell adjacent to the door on the start side), and return true exactly when that cell holds no ball object — using only current-observation reads (`env.grid.get`, `env.width`, `env.height`, cell `type`), guarded against `None` cells, with an expression-only body.

NO CHANGES NEEDED. All five declared propositions have exactly one predicate each with correct names and signatures, using only documented API surface and allowed builtins. blocker_moved correctly checks that no ball occupies any cell adjacent to a door on the start side; has_door_key checks carrying a key matching the door's color; door_open and target_picked_up are proper current-observation conditions with the mission string matched rather than a fixed color; key_lost is a correct event predicate reading the previous valuation without mutation or .get, comparing has_door_key previously against current non-carrying of the matching key and a closed door, and is false on the first step via the emptiness guard.
